thread:
maria (support): FYI - customer acme-inc reported embeddings endpoint throwing 400s and 'embedding dimension mismatch' errors starting ~08:40 PDT. Ticket #4321. They said batch of 8 failed and some requests returned 5xx.

tyler (oncall): Got it, pinging eng-runtime. What's the exact error payload?

maria (support): From their logs:

```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  \"error\": \"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024\",
  \"service\": \"embeddings-v1\"
}
```

maria (support): They also saw latency spikes and an increase in 5xx (~08:35-08:50). Repro command they ran:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"embed-large\",\"input\":[\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"],\"batch_size\":8}'
```

kevin (eng-runtime): Two hypotheses: (1) routing sent requests to a new model variant with 1024-dim embeddings, (2) alias metadata mismatch. Any rollouts in last 24h?

liz (devex): We kicked a canary for embed-large-2 at 06:00, small % traffic. I'll check alias rules now.

liz (devex): Confirmed: at 07:50 we updated the alias mapping but the alias check omitted the embedding_dim tag. That could route some traffic to embed-large-2 which emits 1024 dims.

tyler (oncall): Pagerbot, escalate P1 and page eng-runtime.

pagerbot: @kevin (eng-runtime) you are paged for incident 1893456123 - embeddings dimension mismatch / increased 5xx.

kevin (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. Immediate mitigation: rolling back alias to previous stable variant and draining canary traffic. Starting rollback at 08:55.

maria (support): Customer confirmed at 08:59 that 400s dropped after your rollback, but they still see higher latency on some requests (2x-3x). They want RCA and ETA.

kevin (eng-runtime): Likely cause of latency: batching/backpressure mismatch from the canary variant. It has a larger KV cache init and slower warmup path which increased queueing. Checking metrics.

kevin (eng-runtime): Quick metrics: token latency p50/p95 jumped from ~30ms/60ms to ~90ms/180ms during canary window. Request queue depth increased ~3x. Will investigate batching config and warmup sequence.

liz (devex): I'll draft an interim customer note: short non-technical explanation + we've rolled back the change + we're investigating and will follow up with RCA.

maria (support): Customer asked for repro steps to validate fix. Kevin — what's a minimal safe check they can run?

kevin (eng-runtime): Ask them to run a single-input request against the alias and check returned embedding length. Example:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"embed-large\",\"input\":\"test\"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding | length'
```

kevin (eng-runtime): Expected output after fix: 1536. If 1024, they're still routed to the wrong variant. If 400, capture full response and send.

tyler (oncall): Action items: (1) Confirm rollback fully propagated (liz), (2) run 10m soak and monitor p95 latency/queue depth (kevin), (3) prevent alias->dimension mismatches via a pre-rollout check (liz). ETA: 2h for soak + initial RCA findings.

maria (support): Sent interim message 09:05: \"We rolled back the recent model update; please validate and share results. We'll follow up with a root cause analysis and timeline.\" Customer replied: \"Functionality restored, running our tests now. Thanks.\"

kevin (eng-runtime): Creating PMR stub: will include rollout timeline, config diffs, batching telemetry, and a remediation plan (add pre-deploy metadata checks, integration test, and warmup step for new variants).

liz (devex): Also adding a pipeline gate to verify model metadata (embedding_dim) matches alias expectations before shifting traffic.

maria (support): Will keep ticket open until customer confirms and RCA posted. Linking PMR here once ready.

tyler (oncall): Marking mitigated for now but keep thread open until RCA + tests added.

kevin (eng-runtime): RCA draft uploaded to internal doc (link placeholder). Will follow up with details on batching params and warmup tuning.

maria (support): Thanks all :thumbsup>
